claims.text: Refractory HEAs such as NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 retain unusually high strength at elevated temperatures.
Thermal super-jogging of edge dislocations is the primary mechanism governing elevated-temperature strength retention.
Super-jogged edge dislocations create strong barriers to dislocation motion.
The inhibition of dislocation motion by super-jogged edge dislocations produces an intermediate-temperature yield-strength plateau.
The proposed initial material is a polycrystalline, single-phase refractory HEA.
The as-cast or homogenized initial state has a high density of dislocation structures.
Testing temperature and strain rate should be varied systematically while TEM is used to compare edge and screw dislocations.
The relevant test range extends from room temperature to approximately 1073 K.
Temperatures below approximately 0.6 Tm remain below the diffusion-controlled regime for the proposed alloy.
Edge dislocations develop super-jogged segments that impede subsequent glide.
Edge dislocations can be prevalent and dominant over screw dislocations in a high-temperature-strength BCC alloy.
Thermal activation causes edge dislocations to develop super-jogs that pin them and maintain high internal friction.
At higher temperatures, diffusion-mediated deformation mechanisms soften the alloy.
The HEA will exhibit a yield-strength plateau in an intermediate-temperature interval extending to about 1073 K.
TEM will reveal predominantly edge dislocations with features consistent with thermal super-jogging.
Alloys governed by screw dislocations continuously lose strength with increasing temperature and retain less intermediate-temperature strength.
Plastic flow in elemental and dilute BCC alloys is conventionally controlled by screw-dislocation motion through thermally activated double-kink nucleation.
The proposed mechanism is limited to refractory, high-strength HEAs with high friction stress and prevalent edge-dislocation activity.
Significant short-range ordering or a different dominant dislocation mechanism may invalidate the hypothesis.
Failure to observe both a yield-strength plateau and predominant super-jogged edge dislocations would falsify the hypothesis.
